name: HiJeco generative AI chatbot and AI consultation assistant (Jeju Air)
summary: South Korean low-cost carrier Jeju Air said on November 2 that it is expanding AI in customer service, MoneyToday reported. It introduced an AI consultation assistant for its call center representatives in July last year to help them answer customers faster and more accurately, and it says the average number of inquiries its representatives handled each month from January to September rose 19.9% from the same period a year earlier. Online, it runs 1:1 chat inquiries and HiJeco, a generative AI chatbot that handles consultations in more than 180 languages. The share of foreign-language consultations through HiJeco rose from 14.1% in January to September last year to 23% in the same period this year. Jeju Air also runs quarterly training so representatives can rehearse inquiry scenarios before they happen.

whyItMatters: Every unanswered message is a booking that goes to whoever replies first, and foreign-language travelers are often the ones left waiting. An assistant that helps each agent handle more inquiries, plus a chatbot that answers in the customer's own language around the clock, raises sales without adding headcount. Charter operators and FBOs can do the same at a smaller scale: track how many inquiries go unanswered after hours and in other languages, because that is the revenue an AI front desk can win back.
pricing: Not applicable; Jeju Air's own service
